messages:
Rohan: heads-up: we just saw a rapid preemptible fade in europe-west1 that knocked ~18% of inferencing GPUs -> latency spikes across the dedicated pool. ops-bot alerted at 02:41 UTC.
ops-bot: [ALERT] cluster=rw-eu-west1, pool=infer-dedicated-preemptible, preemptions=68 in 3m, error_rate_up=0.12
Mike: looking at metrics now — p99 token latency jumped from 180ms -> 620ms around 02:40. traces show increased queueing on grpc proxy layer.
Sara: confirmed: autoscaler didn't add on-demand because max_unavailable config blocked scale-up during rolling-drain window. We had max_unavailable=0.1 for the pool.
Jin: that config was to avoid noisy double-scaling for jobs, but in a preemption wave it backfired. We should fallback to on-demand earlier.
Elaine: can we flip routing to the mixed-capacity on-demand-backed pool? I can run the route change and pre-warm a few nodes.
Rohan: do it. Elaine, use the fallback policy "burst_fallback=v2" and route 30% traffic to on-demand initially. Monitor latency.
Elaine: running: `infra-routing set-fallback --pool on-demand-mixed --percent 30 --policy burst_fallback=v2`
Mike: logs: some workloads hit image-pull throttle after flooding new nodes. Reusing cached images is better — starting a local warm cache.
Sara: starting warm cache on 6 nodes: `gcloud compute instances create --image-cache warm-cache --count 6 --zone europe-west1-b` (will add helpers)
Jin: note for postmortem: autoscaler threshold was based on steady-state p95, not short-window p99 spikes. Need a short-window reactive path.
Rohan: Ops decision: immediate mitigation = route 30% -> on-demand-mixed, spin 6 warm nodes, relax max_unavailable to 0.25 for 10m. Longer term: add reactive short-window scale policy.
ops-bot: ACTION: route-change executed by Elaine at 02:44 UTC. Warm nodes requested.
Elaine: route swap completed, traffic shift started. Seeing drop in queue length within 45s. p99 down from 620ms -> 260ms.
Mike: nice. We're still seeing some errors from kv-cache misses where downstream nodes haven't populated KV. Costs will tick up though.
Sara: cost note: this fallback will add ~12% hourly GPU cost for the region if it persists >30m. Let's keep watch and rollback if preempt rates normalize.
Jin: I also created a short-lived policy in runtime: `if preempt_rate > 0.05 for 2m then shift 25% traffic` — testing in canary config.
Rohan: good. Next steps: (1) hold fallback for 15m, (2) collect traces for postmortem, (3) schedule policy change to autoscaler. Who owns postmortem?
Mike: I can own postmortem. Will gather traces, query preempt timelines, and propose conservative reactive thresholds.
Elaine: I'll document the rollback plan and cost impact in the incident doc.
Sara: current numbers: preempt rate dropping to 0.018, p99 steady ~210ms. Trending stable at 02:50.
Rohan: rollback plan ready? Elaine?
Elaine: yes — rolling traffic back over 5m, remove warm nodes after 10m cool-down. Executing rollback now. `infra-routing set-fallback --percent 0 --policy burst_fallback=v2`
ops-bot: ROLLBACK executed at 02:53 UTC by Elaine. Warm nodes scheduled for teardown at 03:05 UTC.
Mike: post-rollback monitoring: p99 stable ~190-220ms, no new preempt bursts.
Jin: noted action items: update autoscaler policy, add warm-image prewarmed pool, introduce short-window preempt detector metric.
Rohan: thanks everyone. We'll run a short postmortem sync at 09:00 and prioritize the autoscaler change for next sprint. Closing thread for now — add findings to #eng-infra-incidents folder. :thumbsup:
